bullets.title: META: Morgan Stanley raises to Top Pick, $10+ EPS upside from AI agents post legal clearing
bullets.body: MS says META could mirror GOOGL's 2H25 trajectory following its $17B legal settlement; Hatch/MetaClaw AI agent launches expected in weeks, adding $10+ EPS potential via agents, Watermelon model, subscriptions, and SMB tools. MS Base Case $775, Bull $1,000; stock trades at 16x EPS, 25% below LT average. Bernstein separately forecasts META surpassing Google Search in ad revenue by end-2026, noting META captured nearly half of every incremental digital ad dollar in Q2.

bullets.title: NVDA: GS flags <10x '28 P/E despite beat/raise; $3.5B MediaTek investment announced
bullets.body: NVDA is down 10 of 12 sessions post-earnings despite GS raising '27 EPS to $16.70 and '28 to $23.00, putting the stock at under 10x '28 estimates. NVDA also announced a $3.5B convertible bond investment in MediaTek, with expanded collaboration on NVLink Fusion and RTX Spark platforms. Memory cost headwinds are compressing gross margins from 75% to 71-72% near-term, per broader memory desk analysis.

bullets.title: AVGO: MS OW reiterated as No. 2 AI Compute pick; AI revenue step to $21.2B OctQ modeled
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley models AVGO AI revenue stepping from $16B in JulQ to $21.2B in OctQ with room for upside. AVGO expected to retain ~80% of the longer-term Google TPU opportunity despite MediaTek/MRVL diversification. Mizuho separately pitches AVGO as a buy into Wednesday earnings on negative sentiment and potential CEO pushback.

bullets.title: MRVL: Google $120B custom silicon deal confirmed as non-aspirational; October analyst day key catalyst
bullets.body: MRVL management confirmed the $120B Google deal is not aspirational; warrant math supports the magnitude. No meaningful Google contribution in FY27, some in FY28, significant from FY29 onward. FY27 revenue guidance raised $500M on supply improvements and custom ramp; FY28 modeled at $18B with >60% YoY datacenter growth. October analyst day expected to provide detailed product and opportunity color.

bullets.title: MU: DRAM +24% Q/Q in August; supply constrained through 2028, 16 multi-year LTAs signed
bullets.body: August DRAM contract pricing +2.2% MoM / +24.0% QoQ; NAND flat MoM / +5.4% QoQ. Memory suppliers meeting only 50-70% of HBM demand with gap widening in 2027. MU signed 16 multi-year LTAs covering ~50% of revenue with take-or-pay and upfront prepayment terms; analyst maintains OW at $1,750 PT (9x FY27E EPS of ~$190). iPhone 18 shipments at risk from DRAM shortages; AAPL smartphone shipments declining L/MSD% YoY in 2026.

bullets.title: AAPL: Tim Cook steps down as CEO; Hedgeye maintains short on services price hikes
bullets.body: Tim Cook's final day as Apple CEO is today; John Ternus takes over tomorrow with an ambitious roadmap including foldable iPhone, smart displays, and AI-powered products. Separately, Hedgeye maintains its short thesis citing Apple TV+ price hikes to $14.99/month and Apple One to $21.95/month; consensus expects iPhone 18 ASP increase of $100-$200 but analyst models only 11% blended ASP improvement. MS notes Mac is Apple's fastest-growing business at +29% YoY to $10.4B, with OpenAI purchasing tens of thousands of Macs for training.

bullets.title: CRM: Salesforce shows strongest NNOAV growth in 4 years; Agentforce customers +70% Q/Q
bullets.body: M³ highlights from Salesforce earnings show the strongest net new on-platform ARV growth in 4 years, with Agentforce customers growing ~70% Q/Q. Analysis concludes AI is additive to software spend, not cannibalistic, validating system-of-record platforms. CRM is also moving Agentforce to usage/outcome-based pricing models per MS TMT note.

bullets.title: PANW: F4Q26 earnings Sept 1; Street at $3.35B revenue, $8.91B ARR; AI/identity traction in focus
bullets.body: Palo Alto Networks reports F4Q26 results September 1. Consensus: $3.35B revenue, $8.913B ARR, 76.1% gross margin, $0.98 EPS. Key investor focus includes firewall refresh demand, CyberArk/Chronosphere contributions, cloud security stability, and AI/agentic identity traction. F1Q27 consensus is $3.222B revenue and $9.215B ARR.

bullets.title: CRWD: Falcon platform now available on Google Cloud; stock +$11 pre-open
bullets.body: CrowdStrike announced pre-market that its Falcon platform is now available on Google Cloud infrastructure. The stock was trading at $229.42, up $11.02 on the news. CRWD is also at a 52-week high, up 105.4% YTD per StreetAccount.

bullets.title: APP: AppLovin eCommerce on track for 11.4K avg stores in 3Q26; global client count at 11.8K
bullets.body: Citi tracks AppLovin Ads at 11,772 global eCommerce clients as of Aug 28, up 1.5% week-over-week. 3Q26 QTD weekly growth averages 1.5%, implying ~11,400 average stores for the quarter. US stores at 5,400 (60.9% Shopify penetration). Store category mix stable.

bullets.title: RBLX: Week 35 CCUs up 1% sequentially at 16.2M; bookings tracking above guidance at $1.68B
bullets.body: Citi (Buy) notes Roblox Week 35 average peak CCUs were 16.2M, up 1% sequentially but down 20% YoY. QTD data implies 3Q26 bookings of $1.68B, above company guidance of $1.65B and Visible Alpha consensus of $1.61B. EU DSA designation (Very Large Online Platform) adds compliance burden.

bullets.title: DKNG: Missouri July handle $247M with 44% share; legal landscape for prediction markets uncertain
bullets.body: DraftKings led Missouri July sports betting with 44% handle share (+4pts MoM) and $109M handle at 13.1% hold rate. FanDuel was second at 27%. Mizuho hosting expert legal call on 9th Circuit ruling implications for prediction markets and DKNG specifically.

bullets.title: AMZN: AWS Saudi Arabia cloud region launching Dec 2026; 50MW AI Zone partnership with HUMAIN
bullets.body: AWS will launch its first Saudi Arabia cloud infrastructure region by December 2026. AWS and HUMAIN (PIF-owned) will provide up to 50MW capacity in Saudi Arabia's first AI Zone by 2028, including AWS Trainium chips and latest NVIDIA AI infrastructure. AWS is HUMAIN's preferred AI partner.

bullets.title: Hedgeye Risk Ranges: MSFT, AAPL, AMZN, NVDA bullish; META, GOOGL, TSLA bearish
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Aug 31 signal update shows MSFT (buy range $479-516), AAPL ($306-324), AMZN ($256-270), NVDA ($209-229), and NFLX ($78-83) all bullish. META ($532-588), GOOGL ($337-350), and TSLA ($334-365) remain bearish. SNDK shifted from bearish to neutral; ORCL removed. Separately, Hedgeye's macro show notes AMZN as Friday's best large-cap opportunity and reiterates MSFT as a long after prior short pivot.

bullets.title: PINS: Mizuho Outperform / $32 PT; CFO resignation hits stock -3.9% pre-market
bullets.body: Mizuho maintains Outperform on Pinterest with a $32 PT and is hosting a small group call with Pinterest IR on 9/11. Pinterest's CFO resigned, sending shares down 3.9% pre-market. Pinterest market cap is $13.5B.

bullets.title: NVDA in talks to acquire Hugging Face at $13B+ valuation
bullets.body: Per StreetAccount M&A weekly summary, Nvidia is in 'serious' talks to acquire Hugging Face at a valuation exceeding $13B. The deal would position NVDA as an AI platform leader with a major AI software/model hub, extending well beyond its hardware franchise.

bullets.title: TSLA vs BYD: BYD Q2 operating margin 5.4% vs TSLA 1.4%; profitability gap widening
bullets.body: BYD's Q2 2026 operating margin of 5.4% materially exceeds Tesla's 1.4%, with BYD's H1 2026 margin at 4.2% up 1.9pp YoY. Comparison excludes extraordinary government subsidies beyond industry-standard support. TSLA also screens bearish in Hedgeye risk ranges ($334-365).

bullets.title: CLS: UBS channel checks show 1.6T switches have better margins than 800G; AI volumes ramping faster than expected
bullets.body: UBS notes Celestica channel checks show 1.6T switches carry better margins than 800G, and AI program volumes are ramping faster than expected, supporting UBS's 31% 2028 revenue growth forecast. JBL Trainium shipments expected to grow from 1.8M units in 2026 to 2.8M in 2027 on Amazon ramp.

bullets.title: SNAP/TTD: Pre-market movers on advertising strength; TTD +3.8%, SNAP +2.4%
bullets.body: Per StreetAccount pre-market summary, The Trade Desk rose 3.8% and Snap rose 2.4% in pre-market trading, both attributed to advertising-related strength. No specific analyst actions cited in the summary.

bullets.title: NXST: Citi maintains Buy, $215 PT; legal catalysts expected 4Q26-1Q27
bullets.body: Citi highlights Nexstar as a top TMT conference idea with a Buy rating and $215 PT. Legal catalysts expected in 4Q26 to 1Q27, or potential settlement. Nexstar is flagged as a favorable risk/reward setup into the Citi 2026 Global TMT Conference (September 8-10).
